case_name: Bhawani Prasad Sonkar v Union Of India & Ors.
facts: Appellant's father was posted as a Guard Mail/Express at Lucknow Junction.
Appellant's father appeared before the Medical Board and was declared medically unfit in A2, A3, B1 and B2 categories.
Appellant's father was found fit in category C1 and C2 and directed to appear for another medical examination after six months.
Appellant's father again appeared for a medical examination and was declared medically unfit as de-categorized employee.
Appellant's father was retired from service vide retirement order dated 30th August, 1999 issued by respondent No.3 viz. Divisional Railways Manager (Karmik), Lucknow.
Appellant moved an application dated 1st September, 1999 before respondent No.2 requesting that his son be given compassionate appointment as a Class IV employee.
Appellant's father moved another application, dated 30th December, 1999, before respondent No.3.

Railway Board issued a letter stating that when an employee is declared as medically unfit to perform the work which he was performing but is found to be fit to perform work in a lower category, any request for giving compassionate employment to such employee's ward would not be considered if the employee opts for voluntary retirement after being de-categorized.

Respondent No.3 issued a letter dated 15th February, 2002 to appellant's father stating that the application for appointment of his son on compassionate ground was not found fit for consideration by the competent authority.
issues: Whether the appellant is eligible for compassionate appointment in view of the Railway Board Circular dated 29.11.2001.
Whether the appellant's father was forced to retire and whether this fact can be taken into account while considering the claim for compassionate appointment.
petitioner_arguments: Appellant's father retired without being offered a suitable alternative job, despite being found medically fit in category B1.
The respondents are obliged to appoint the appellant in terms of instructions dated 7th April, 1983 and 3rd September, 1983, which were reiterated in Circular dated 22nd September, 1995.
respondent_arguments: Appellant's father opted for voluntary retirement in terms of the Railway Board's letter dated 18th January, 2000.
The appellant has not brought any material on record to substantiate his plea that his father was forced to retire.
court_reasoning: Compassionate employment is given solely on humanitarian grounds with the sole object to provide immediate relief to the employee's family to tide over the sudden financial crisis and cannot be claimed as a matter of right.
The scheme or policy, as the case may be, is binding both on the employer and the employee.
A compassionate appointment cannot be claimed as a matter of course or in posts above Class III and IV.
holding: The appeal is dismissed. The appellant's claim for compassionate appointment is not eligible under the Railway Board Circular dated 29.11.2001.
